$comment: The scene event contract: every built-in event name, what it carries, who may emit it and what a host does with it. Source of truth for frameos/tools/generate_events_contract.py, which writes the Nim, C, TypeScript and Python tables and the editor catalog (frontend/schema/events.json). The prose is docs/events.md; the conformance corpus every runner must pass is docs/event-fixtures.json. Add an event HERE, regenerate, add a fixture — never to one of the generated files.

origins.driver: An input driver on the frame (evdev, gpioButton, the ESP32 button task).
origins.preview: The browser preview's canvas and buttons.
origins.schedule: A schedule entry firing on the frame.
origins.http:write: The frame's HTTP API with the frame access key (or `public` access): POST /event/<name>.
origins.http:admin: The frame's HTTP API with an admin session or the serverApiKey bearer — the self-hosted backend.
origins.cloud: FrameOS Cloud, through a hub verb.
origins.system: The runtime itself: boot, the portal, settings apply, device flow.

classes.lifecycle: Sent by the host to a scene as it is loaded, shown, rendered and left.
classes.input: Something a person did: a key, a pointer, a button.
classes.scene-command: Asks the host to do something for the current scene; a scene may dispatch it.
classes.device-command: Asks the runtime to do something to the device. Never delivered to a scene, never offered by the editor.

customEvents.$comment: A name that is not in `events` is a custom scene event (a scene's `customEvents`). Every host delivers it to the current scene's listeners of that name. `origins` is who may always send one; `declarableOrigins` are the ones a scene opts into per event, with `origins` on its declaration (`{name: "nextPage", origins: ["schedule"]}`).

pointer.$comment: Driver / preview -> host: both axes 0..wireMax across the panel, whatever the device reports. The host scales into scene pixels before a scene sees it.

context.$comment: The `context` object JavaScript sees. `sandboxes` says where a key exists: a code node (one expression) or an app (a module).

keys.name: event
keys.description: The name of the event this run is handling.

keys.name: loopIndex
keys.description: Index of the current iteration inside a loop.

keys.name: loopKey
keys.description: Key of the current iteration inside a loop.

keys.name: hasImage
keys.description: Whether the run carries a canvas.

keys.name: image
keys.description: The canvas, when there is one.

keys.name: imageWidth
keys.description: Width of the canvas. In scene pixels, of the canvas this run draws on (a cell's inside render/split); absent when the run has none.

keys.name: imageHeight
keys.description: Height of the canvas. In scene pixels, of the canvas this run draws on (a cell's inside render/split); absent when the run has none.

logEvents.$comment: Log lines (not scene events) a control plane derives state from. `sceneChanged`: the frame now shows `sceneId`. `sceneStateChanged`: re-read the frame's state.

events.name: init
events.description: Once per scene, when it is first loaded and its apps are ready — before its first open and render.

events.name: render
events.description: Render the scene. Triggered according to the frame's refresh interval, or when explicitly requested.

events.name: open
events.description: Every time the scene becomes the frame's current scene: at boot, and whenever the frame switches to it, including switching back.

events.name: close
events.description: When the frame switches away from the scene to another one. Carries no payload.

events.name: keyDown
events.description: When a key is pressed on a keyboard

events.name: keyUp
events.description: When a key is released on a keyboard

events.name: mouseMove
events.description: When a mouse moves (not logged)

events.name: mouseDown
events.description: When a mouse button is pressed (not logged)

events.name: mouseUp
events.description: When a mouse button is released (not logged)

events.name: wheel
events.description: When a mouse wheel is scrolled (not logged). Deltas are wheel notches; deltaY is positive when scrolling down (towards the user), deltaX when scrolling right. Linux frames only.

events.name: turnOn
events.description: Turn the screen on

events.name: turnOff
events.description: Turn the screen off

events.name: button
events.description: When a GPIO button is pressed

events.name: setSceneState
events.description: Set the scene's public state. This is not used for private state changes.

events.name: setCurrentScene
events.description: Switch the frame to another scene. An optional `state` object is applied to that scene's public state.

events.name: metrics
events.description: Log the frame's metrics now.

events.name: reload
events.description: Re-read the frame's configuration and scenes from disk.

events.name: restart
events.description: Exit and relaunch the FrameOS runtime.

schedule.label: Restart FrameOS
schedule.description: Exit and relaunch the FrameOS runtime. A few seconds of downtime; the device stays up.

events.name: reboot
events.description: Reboot the whole device.

schedule.label: Reboot device
schedule.description: Reboot the whole device. Use this for the nightly reboot some panels and Wi-Fi chips like.

events.name: uploadScenes
events.description: Replace the frame's uploaded scenes.
